quotes.text: Filing friction is a silent killer of innovation because it forces you to be a librarian when you should be a creator.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the hidden productivity cost of folder-based filing in one memorable image.

quotes.text: Rigid directories try to force a one-to-one relationship on a many-to-many world and that is exactly where the model breaks.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains precisely why hierarchical folders fail for documents that matter to several teams.

quotes.text: When you save a file, the graph doesn't just record the file name. It maps that document into a multidimensional mathematical space.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear plain-language explanation of how the semantic index represents documents.

quotes.text: Manual tagging was a failed experiment because it required humans to act like machines, and we have finally stopped asking people to do what software does better.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for automated metadata extraction over manual tagging.

quotes.text: If the executives are still emailing attachments and asking for the latest version in a specific folder, the graph will fail.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights that leadership behaviour decides whether a graph-based architecture is adopted.

chapters.title: Microsoft Graph and the semantic index

takeaways: Deep folder hierarchies impose a navigational tax because users must recall where someone else once decided a file belongs.
Microsoft Graph and the semantic index locate content by meaning, relationships and context instead of by its storage path.
Moving beyond folders is a cultural change that needs automated metadata, query-based training and leaders who model the new behaviour.
hook: Knowledge workers lose a large share of their day hunting through nested folders that force every document into a single place. This episode is for Microsoft 365 architects and IT leaders who want to understand how Microsoft Graph, the semantic index and SharePoint Premium replace static hierarchies with context-driven findability, and how to bring users along.
